harness: Kilo Code (VS Code extension `kilocode.Kilo-Code`) — Roo Code fork, now a Kilo/OpenCode-v2 core rewrite; also ships a JetBrains plugin and a standalone `kilo` CLI
vendor: Kilo Code (Kilo-Org / publisher `kilocode`); core is an OpenCode fork (README credits anomalyco/opencode); cloud/app.kilo.ai optional, all local data is first-party
repo: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode (monorepo; packages/core = Kilo v2 engine, packages/kilo-vscode = VS Code ext, packages/schema = wire types, packages/kilo-docs)
surfaces: VS Code extension panel + webview (`kilocode.Kilo-Code` v7.8.15, publisher `kilocode`); JetBrains plugin (plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/28350-kilo-code); standalone CLI/TUI (`kilo`, npm `@kilocode/cli`); `kilo serve` local HTTP server; cloud app (app.kilo.ai). The VS Code extension is a thin client: it spawns the bundled `kilo.exe serve --port 0` child process with a random `KILO_SERVER_PASSWORD` and talks to it over HTTP, so ALL session state lives in the CLI/core database.
binaries: `kilo.exe` — bundled with the extension at `<extensionPath>\bin\kilo.exe` (spawned as `kilo serve --port 0`); npm `@kilocode/cli` installs `kilo`; subcommands `kilo db path`, `kilo db "<SQL>" --format json`, `kilo serve`, `kilo export <ses_id>`, `kilo session list --format json`

paths: %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\kilo.db  (PRIMARY, current upstream code path: Global.Path.data = xdgData + "kilo"; xdg-basedir@5.1.0 has no win32 special case, so ~/.local/share is used on Windows too; upstream docs table lists exactly this for Windows)
%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\kilo-<channel>.db  (dev-channel DBs; the VS Code extension sets KILO_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB=true so it always uses kilo.db)
%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\storage\  (PRE-7.0.26 flat-file data dir, migrated into SQLite on first run; read-only legacy)
%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\log\*.log  (plain-text debug logs, rotating, 50MB x10; format `LEVEL <iso-ts> +Xms key=value msg`; NOT usable as an activity feed — DEBUG level can contain prompts)

%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\kilocode.kilo-code\tasks\<taskId>\api_conversation_history.json  (LEGACY pre-v7 extension layout: JSON array, whole-file rewrite; read-only import source, no longer written)
%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\kilocode.kilo-code\tasks\<taskId>\history_item.json  (legacy per-task metadata: task title, workspace, ts, mode, rootTaskId, parentTaskId)

%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\roovscode.roo-cline\tasks\  (Roo Code import root, one of 5 upstream-listed roots: roovscode.roo-cline, roovscode.roo-code, rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline, rooveterinaryinc.roo-code, rooveterinaryinc.roo-code-nightly)

%APPDATA%\kilo\kilo.db  (DISPUTED — upstream CHANGELOG 7.0.26/7.0.27 says "deleting ~/.local/share/kilo/kilo.db* files (%APPDATA% on windows)"; current code says %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo. Probe both, plus %LOCALAPPDATA%\kilo\kilo.db)
storage.format: SQLite 3 database in WAL mode (binary container, NOT encrypted, no auth token needed for read access; `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`). Tables: session(id, project_id, parent_id, slug, directory, path, title, agent, model JSON {id,providerID,variant?}, time_created, time_updated, ...), session_message(id, session_id, type, seq, time_created, data JSON), message(id, session_id, time_created, data JSON), part(id, message_id, session_id, time_created, data JSON), event(id, aggregate_id=sessionID, seq, type, data JSON), event_sequence, project, project_directory, todo, credential, account. Per-row JSON blobs in `data` TEXT columns hold the actual records (tool parts, assistant text, prompts). Legacy pre-7.0 format was JSON-per-file (api_conversation_history.json / ui_messages.json / _index.json), now read-only import material.
storage.append_semantics: NOT a tailable text log. Rows are INSERTed/UPDATEd live while the agent works (projector upserts session_message / message / part rows per streamed event, and the `event` table is an append-only durable log with a monotonic per-session `seq`). The DB *file* however is rewritten by SQLite in WAL mode with periodic checkpoints, so Discodex's byte-offset LogTailer cannot read it — a row-level reader keyed on (aggregate_id|session_id, seq) is required, plus a snapshot/copy strategy for WAL.
storage.session_file_naming: No per-session files. Ids: session `ses_...` (SessionID), message `msg_...` (schema-enforced prefix, monotonic), tool call ids are opaque `callID` strings. Tool `name` values seen upstream: read, write, edit, bash, grep, glob, apply_patch, webfetch, websearch, todowrite, question, skill, task.

fields.project: `session.directory` (absolute workspace dir) → basename only, e.g. "Discodex"; also `project.name`/`project.worktree` tables. Legacy equivalent: history_item.json `workspace`.
fields.model: `session.model` = JSON `{id, providerID, variant?}` → e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-5"; per-message `assistant.model` (Model.Ref) and durable event `session.next.model.switched` also carry it.
fields.file_basename: Tool part `state.input.path` (read/write/edit/apply_patch) → basename only (e.g. "provider.rs"); `state.input.outputPaths` also exist. grep/glob carry a search *directory* in `path`, so the basename rule must be restricted to file-mutating/reading tools.
fields.tool_activity: Tool `name` + `state.input` → fixed label via existing `classify_tool()`: edit/write/apply_patch→"Editing files", read→"Reading project files", grep/glob→"Searching project", bash→command-sniffed label ("Running Rust tests", "Building Rust project", …), webfetch→"Browsing documentation", todowrite→"Planning changes". The raw command/args are inspected locally only and never published.
fields.phase: Derived from tool-part status (pending/running → RunningTools; completed/error → back to Thinking) plus turn boundaries (`session.next.step.ended` → Completed, `session.next.text.ended` → TerminalCandidate).

parser_strategy:
TWO STAGES.

Stage A — new reader (not a tailer). `KiloDbReader` (new module, e.g. src/kilo_db.rs): open the DB read-only via a new `rusqlite` dependency. Because the DB is WAL and concurrently written by the `kilo serve` child process, use the safe pattern: copy `kilo.db` + `kilo.db-wal` (+ `-shm`) to a temp snapshot on each poll and query the copy (avoids SQLITE_BUSY and the read-only-WAL recovery failure); fall back to an in-place read-only open (`mode=ro`, `busy_timeout`) when the copy path fails. Poll every ~1.5 s. Queries: `SELECT aggregate_id, seq, type, data FROM event WHERE aggregate_id=? AND seq>? ORDER BY seq` (durable event log, aggregate = sessionID) and `SELECT session_id, seq, type, data FROM session_message WHERE session_id=? AND seq>? ORDER BY seq` (canonical message stream), plus `SELECT id, directory, model, agent FROM session WHERE id=?` for metadata. Emit each row as a canonical JSON line so the existing `parse_line_for` contract is reused: {"kind":"event"|"message"|"session","type":<row type>,"data":<parsed JSON>,"seq":<seq>,"session_id":<id>}. Because the assistant `session_message` row is UPDATEd in place, the reader must DIFF per-call-id tool states across polls (same call_id tracking as Codex/DSH), not rely on row growth.

Stage B — events.rs parser. Add `Provider::KiloCode => parse_kilo_line(line)` to `parse_line_for`; it parses the canonical JSON and maps:
- session row → SessionMetadata{project: basename(directory), cwd: directory} + AgentDetected{agent: model.id} (validated charset).
- event "session.next.prompted" → TaskStarted{started_at_ms: data.timestamp}; `data.prompt` is never read.
- event "session.next.tool.called" → TrackedToolStarted{call_id: data.callID, activity:{label: classify_tool(data.tool, input.command), file: extract_file_basename(input) (only "path"), language: language_from_file(file)}}. `input.command` is scanned locally for the label only.
- event "session.next.tool.success" | "session.next.tool.failed" → TrackedToolFinished{call_id: data.callID} (result/content/error never read).
- event "session.next.shell.started" → TrackedToolStarted{call_id: data.callID, activity:{label: classify_tool("bash", data.command)}} (command never emitted).
- event "session.next.reasoning.started" → Thinking{reasoning: None} (reasoning text never read).
- event "session.next.text.ended" → TerminalCandidate; event "session.next.step.ended" → Completed.
- event "session.next.agent.switched" → AgentDetected{agent: data.agent}; "session.next.model.switched" → AgentDetected{agent: data.model.id}.
- message row type "user" → TaskStarted{started_at_ms: data.time.created}; type "assistant" → per content item: type "tool" with state.status pending/running → TrackedToolStarted{id: content.id}; completed/error → TrackedToolFinished{id: content.id}; type "reasoning" → Thinking{None}; type "text" → TerminalCandidate.
Unknown type, unparsable JSON, missing fields → no events (fail-safe, no Discord noise).

risks: NEW DEPENDENCY: reading SQLite from Rust requires rusqlite (or similar) — a new crate + bundled-SQLite build (binary size) or a system-SQLite requirement. Flagged as required cost; there is no way to read this format with the current dependency set.

FORMAT MISMATCH WITH THE ADAPTER CONTRACT: Discodex's LogTailer is byte-offset/append-only JSONL. A SQLite file cannot be tailed; the adapter needs a row-level reader with seq watermarks, per-call-id state diffing (the assistant row is UPDATEd in place), and a different keying scheme for ActivityState (PathBuf keyed).

CONCURRENT WRITER: the DB is written by the `kilo serve` child process in WAL mode. A naive read-only open can hit SQLITE_BUSY or WAL-recovery write failures; the snapshot-copy (kilo.db + -wal) approach is required, with a busy timeout and retry/backoff.

SCHEMA CHURN: upstream shipped ~50 migrations in 2026 alone; table/column renames and JSON shape changes are frequent (e.g. state.input String→object, media/file tool-content variants pre-1.17.13). Requires runtime schema probing and fail-safe disablement.

PRIVACY: the DB stores full prompts, assistant text, reasoning and tool results. Only fixed labels + basenames + model ids may leave the machine; any future change that echoes `data`/`result`/`content`/`prompt` would leak. Mandatory privacy unit tests needed.

DUPLICATE/NOISY SESSIONS: the same kilo.db is shared by the standalone `kilo` CLI, the JetBrains plugin and the VS Code extension, and it retains finished sessions — without an "active session" filter Discodex would replay old sessions and could publish stale presence.

PATH AMBIGUITY: upstream code resolves %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\kilo.db while CHANGELOG 7.0.26/7.0.27 mentions %APPDATA% on Windows; the resolver must probe candidates rather than hardcode one. Also VS Code Remote SSH moves the DB to the remote host, and %USERPROFILE% differs per profile.
CLOUD SESSIONS ARE NOT LOCAL: app.kilo.ai cloud sessions are not in the local DB unless imported, so cloud-only runs are invisible to a local adapter.

LOG FILE IS A TRAP: %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\log\*.log is plain text and looks tailable, but at DEBUG level it can contain prompt/tool output — parsing it would violate the privacy rules. Must not be used.

LEGACY GLOBALSTORAGE IS A DEAD END: the old tasks/<id>/api_conversation_history.json layout is JSON-array-per-file rewritten wholesale (not append-only) and is only a migration source; it also would be skipped by Discodex's discovery because watcher::collect_logs skips directories named "tasks".

EXTENSION-SIDE AUTH: the `kilo serve` HTTP API requires KILO_SERVER_PASSWORD (random per extension-host session), so the HTTP route is NOT usable by an external watcher; only direct DB access is token-free.

summary:
Kilo Code DOES keep a rich local, unencrypted, machine-readable activity record — but not in a tailable log. Current Kilo (v7.x, the `kilocode.Kolo-Code` VS Code extension + the `kilo` CLI it spawns) stores ALL session state in one SQLite database, `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\kilo\kilo.db` (WAL mode). The DB contains everything Discodex needs — workspace directory, model id, live tool calls with their arguments (including file paths), tool results, turn/step boundaries and millisecond timestamps — in `session`, `session_message` and `event` tables whose `data` columns hold JSON blobs. The `event` table is effectively an append-only, per-session-ordered durable event log (`aggregate_id` = session id, monotonic `seq`, types like `session.next.tool.called` / `.success` / `.failed`), and `session_message` is the canonical ordered message stream (type + seq + JSON with assistant tool parts carrying `state.status`, `state.input`, `time.created`).

Consequences for Discodex: the existing append-only-JSONL `LogTailer` + `parse_line_for` contract CANNOT read it (no byte-offset tailing, no per-line records). An adapter is still viable but needs a new ingestion path: a `rusqlite`-backed row reader (new dependency), a per-session `seq` watermark, snapshot-copy of `kilo.db`+`-wal` to dodge SQLite locking/WAL-readonly issues, and per-call-id state diffing because the assistant row is UPDATEd in place while streaming. No encryption and no auth token are required for DB read access (the alternative HTTP route, `kilo serve`, requires a random `KILO_SERVER_PASSWORD` and is therefore unusable). Legacy pre-7.0 installs still have `%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\kilocode.kilo-code\tasks\<id>\api_conversation_history.json` (JSON array, rewritten wholesale, read-only import source) — JSON-per-file, not append-only, and Discodex's discovery skips directories named `tasks` anyway. Verdict: the on-disk data is rich enough for Codex/DSH-level presence (project, model, file basename, tool label, phase, timer), but only via a SQLite poller, i.e. a materially different adapter — hence "partial" rather than "rich". Cloud sessions are not in the local DB.
